Install the tool

This lesson is fixture content. It stands in for a real lesson so that the checks which walk a content tree have something to walk. Read it as a shape rather than as instruction.

A lesson body is a fragment of HTML. Code appears in a pre element that carries a data-lang attribute, and the attribute tells the checks how to treat the block. A block of commands is one thing, and a transcript of what those commands printed is another, so the two never share a language.

Start by asking the tool which version you have. The command below prints one line, and the block after it records that line.

$ example-tool --version
example-tool 1.4.0

Output belongs to the command above it. That is the rule the pairing check enforces, and it is why an output block that opens a lesson is reported: nothing precedes it, so a reader cannot tell what produced it.

Now list the plugins the tool found. Two commands in a row are fine, and so is a single transcript that answers the second one.

$ example-tool plugins list
NAME        VERSION   STATUS
linter      0.9.2     enabled
formatter   0.4.1     enabled

For the wider background, see the tool documentation. The link checks resolve prose links like that one, and they need the network, so they run in their own tier rather than on every pull request.
